note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 58; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 2 with the calculator, S2) on data/benches/prepare.json: a standard solution planned with the calculator, weighed and made up, and its concentration worked out from what the balance read.
title: Experiment: a solution by calculation

steps.title: The crystals' molar mass
steps.text: Open the notebook and its calculator. Choose "molar mass", click the formula's field and type CuSO4.5H2O: the blue crystals, five waters to each copper sulfate.
steps.why: A molar mass is the sum of its atoms' atomic weights: one copper, one sulfur, nine oxygens and ten hydrogens make 249.68 g/mol. The water in the crystals counts.

steps.title: How much to weigh
steps.text: Choose "solution": type CuSO4.5H2O, then 0.0500 (mol/L), then 100 (mL). Click "write m in the notebook", and close the notebook.
steps.why: m = c V M: 0.0500 mol/L in 0.100 L is 0.00500 mol, and 0.00500 mol of the crystals weigh 1.248 g.

steps.title: The flask on the balance
steps.text: Click the first volumetric flask to pick it up, then click the balance. Then right-click the balance and click "tare".
steps.why: A volumetric flask holds its nominal volume at its mark, to within its class: 100 mL within 0.10 mL. Tared, the balance reads only what goes into it.

checks.text: the flask tared on the balance

steps.title: About 1.25 g of the crystals
steps.text: Pick up the jar, then right-click the flask for the menu. Type 1.25, then click "tip 1.25 g of the solid". Write down what the balance reads.
steps.why: Copper sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO4.5H2O, is 249.69 g a mole: 2.5 g of it is about 0.0100 mol. The balance's reading, not the 2.5, is what you took.

steps.title: What the balance says
steps.text: Right-click the balance and click "+ mass": what you actually took, never quite what you aimed at.
steps.why: A hand tips about what it aims at; the balance says what it was, to 0.1 mg. Planning gives the aim; the balance gives the number to work with.

steps.title: Water to dissolve them
steps.text: Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask, type 50 and click "pour". Then right-click the flask, click "stir", and click 60x on the clock.
steps.why: A solid dissolves in some of the water first; the flask is made up to its mark only once it has, or the volume would change as it dissolved.

steps.title: Until it is dissolved
steps.text: Watch the blue crystals go into the water.

steps.title: To the mark
steps.text: Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask and click "to the mark".
steps.why: The bottom of the meniscus on the mark: the flask now holds its own 100 mL (within 0.10 mL) of a solution of all the copper sulfate you weighed. Its concentration is the moles you weighed over 0.1000 L.

steps.title: The moles you weighed
steps.text: Open the notebook's calculator, choose "moles": type CuSO4.5H2O and the balance's reading (from the notebook's table). The concentration is those moles in the flask's 0.100 L.
steps.why: n = m / M, and c = n / V: what you weighed, not what you planned.

report.label: the concentration you made
report.why: c = m / (M V): the balance's reading over 249.68 g/mol, in the flask's 0.100 L. Your hand tipped about what it aimed at, so the concentration is near 0.0500 mol/L, not on it; the balance reads within 0.2 mg and the flask holds its own volume within 0.1 mL.
